summary: Fallback routing supersedes active version pin during canary weight update (priority inversion)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexaHealth reported that after they started a canary rollout (adjusting canary weight from 0% to 10%) for gpt-medium-v3.1, a subset of requests that had explicit model version pins continued to route to the fallback quantized model (gpt-medium-v3.1-fallback-quant) instead of the pinned version. This occurred even though the pinned version remained healthy and dedicated pool capacity was available.

Impact:
- Some pinned requests from LexaHealth experienced output format changes and slight regressions because the fallback model is quantized and tuned differently.
- Customer telemetry and downstream processing saw ~7% degraded correctness on pinned workloads during the window.
- Business impact: potential SLA blip for Dedicated customer.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated cluster: prod-us-east
- Customer workspace: lexah-health-prod (dedicated pool)
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer pins requests in their integration header: X-Redwood-Model-Pin: gpt-medium-v3.1
2) Start a canary via Console: set canary weight for gpt-medium-v3.1 -> 10% with fallback variant configured (gpt-medium-v3.1-fallback-quant)
3) Observe routing logs and sampled traces for pinned request IDs in the time window when weight was adjusted

Observed behavior:
- 6:42:12 UTC: weight change applied in console
- 6:42:12-6:43:05 UTC: ~7% of pinned requests routed to fallback variant
- Traces show routing decision path: route-eval -> weight-based assignment -> fallback-path selected (unexpected)

Expected behavior:
- Requests with explicit model pin must always route to the pinned model if the pinned model is healthy and has capacity, regardless of canary weight adjustments or fallback configuration.
logs_and_evidence:
- Example request ids: req_0a7f3c, req_0a9d12, req_0b3f88
- Traces: trace.us-east.0a7f3c -> routing_decision: pin=true, runtime_decision=fallback_selected
- Console change audit: /api/rollouts/12345 PATCH by lexah-admin at 2026-03-10T06:42:12Z
- Metrics: routing_rule_mismatch{project=lexah,region=us-east} count=83 in 53s window
- Heapster logs: routing-engine INFO "evaluated candidates; preferred:fallback; reason:score_override"
- Screenshot of Console rollout adjustment attached (not in JSON)

investigation: Initial hypothesis: capacity-driven fallback - rejected. No capacity shortage or 5xxs in serving logs.

Routing engine logging showed a new field 'score_override' which was set when canary weights were updated; comparator ordering allowed 'score_override' to win over explicit pin flag in rare interleavings.

Reproduced in staging by applying a weight change and firing pinned requests in the exact ordering; root cause reproduced deterministically with a pause between write to routing-config and config-index update.
Code area: routing/decision/comparator.go - pin precedence check occurred after score override logic rather than before; comparator is non-atomic with concurrent config refresh path.
SRE confirmed no impact to other customers in the cluster; effect limited to requests using explicit model pin headers during canary weight adjustments.
Added additional telemetry to measure 'pin-honored' boolean on routing decisions to monitor regressions.
resolution:
Fix and workaround:
- Immediate workaround used by Support: requested customer to pause canary weight changes until hotfix applied, or temporarily set explicit model-pin lock via Console that enforces 'pin_lock=true'.
- Hotfix applied: routing comparator change and additional unit + integration tests merged in PR #6123 and deployed as routing-service v1.23.4 to prod-us-east on 2026-03-11 at 12:50 UTC.
- Post-deploy verification: replays of sampled traffic and customer test suite show 0 mismatches in subsequent 24h window.

Follow-ups and action items:
- Add automated e2e test covering pin + canary weight change race (assigned to Diego).
- Instrumentation: emit gauge 'routing.pin_precedence_violations' and alert if >0 in 5m window (assigned to SRE).
- Console UX: add warning when starting a canary if active pinned routes are detected (product ticket created).
- Postmortem recorded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEV/2026-03-10+LexaHealth+canary+routing+postmortem
